price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: outcome-derived possession labels and mechanical floors
methodological_questions: Is the opponent T+1 PPP shift after play type X large enough, relative to direct PPP gaps and label thresholds, to change AVOID labels?
Do own-team lag-k effects survive team-season (within-team) baselines and decay as an action-memory effect should?
Are downstream and lag effects produced by labelling, foul-bucket, outcome-conditioning or team-quality artifacts?

historical_evidence.finding: Extended Possession Value: opponent T+1 suppression judged real for 4/8 play types (CUT +0.0220, TRANSITION +0.0145, SPOT_UP +0.0124, POST_UP +0.0194); DRIVE not real (opp ATT +0.0024). Recorded evidence: downstream effects are small (~0.01-0.02 PPP) relative to direct PPP gaps; player-level downstream mostly non-FINDING after BH.

Descriptive: possession ending state shifts opponent output over the next 90-180s mainly through volume (dOppPoss), not PPP; live turnover raises opponent points +0.510 over 90s (dOppPPP +0.055, dOppPoss +0.298). Record notes ~0.01-0.02 PPP boundary drift and that the live-TO volume effect is largely definitional. No inferential tests.

Own-team lag curves: global lifts (e.g., SPOT_UP lag-1 +0.027) were flat/non-decaying and vanished after team-season demeaning; within-team memory essentially none except SPOT_UP lag-1 (PNR lag-1 within-team lift -0.0218).

Level 1 gate on cross-possession memory FAILED decay-sanity (DRIVE lifts flat +0.015 to +0.021; within-team +0.015 to -0.002); Cohen d ~0.01-0.03 with p~0 from n>150k; callable play-type horizons = 0; team-quality confound.

Labeling audit: OTHER has 36% foul endings with inflated PPP; DRIVE sits 12pp below the foul benchmark (foul leakage); PNR shows 22% foul rate; initiation_type maps only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) to a real play type.

After the opponent runs/succeeds with X, a 'defensive aftershock' (~+0.12 to +0.135 next-possession PPP premium) replicated for 8/8 play types in all games and playoffs. This tests a differently defined contrast (next offensive play type vs its baseline, after success), not the same estimand.
Star-level sequential suppression by preceding opponent play type (e.g., PUTBACK top suppressor for 6+ stars) with min n_after 30-95 and no multiplicity correction; failure evidence recorded.
Star suppression profiles incl. preceding opponent play type: rank-1 deltas mostly within 1-2 SE, no multiple-comparison control, OTHER artifact flagged.
Brown-initiated possession to Tatum next-possession ATT: CIs include zero, real ATT inside placebo range, signs flip across quarters and RS/PO (treated n=1173).
On-ball coverage labels from NBA matchup/PBP feeds reached only 14.9% and 3.3% confident labeling; switches_on unpopulated (relevant only as a caution on label quality).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Global (pooled) own-team lag-1 to lag-5 lift curves as evidence of action memory
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: flat non-decaying global lifts disappear after team-season demeaning.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Level 1 decay-sanity gate for cross-possession memory
failed_approaches.why: Recorded failure: lifts flat, team-quality confound; callable play-type horizons = 0; significance driven by n>150k with d~0.01-0.03.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using raw play-type PPP (OTHER, DRIVE) as clean efficiency labels
failed_approaches.why: Recorded labelling artifact: foul-ending leakage and only 0.7% initiation_type mapping.
Recorded: no multiplicity correction; small n_after cells (32-95) vs large baselines.
Recorded: deltas mostly within 1-2 SE, no multiple-comparison control.

evidence_establishes: Per FAM:SF-APPS-075, the recorded opponent T+1 suppression for play types is small (~0.01-0.02 PPP) relative to direct PPP gaps, and is real for only 4/8 play types.
Per FAM:SF-APPS-073 and FAM:SF-CHT-029 (both 'artifact'), own-sequence lag effects collapse under within-team baselines; the only surviving within-team memory recorded is SPOT_UP lag-1.
Per FAM:SF-CHT-025, play-type PPP labels carry foul-bucket/leakage artifacts that can distort any label-threshold analysis (OTHER, DRIVE).
Per FAM:SF-APPS-078, apparent downstream cost of a possession ending state operates mostly via opponent possession volume and is partly definitional.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether any specific AVOID-label threshold would flip when downstream T+1 PPP is added; no retrieved record states an AVOID rule or tests flip rates.
Whether downstream effects are causal (not just conditioned on outcome/team quality); FAM:SF-APPS-075 is recorded as 'not a hypothesis test' and its controls are not visible in the retrieved text.
Reconciliation of the small ~0.01-0.02 T+1 suppression (FAM:SF-APPS-075) with the ~+0.12 aftershock in FAM:SF07, which uses a different estimand.
Behaviour on 2025-26 data, which is not covered by any retrieved record.
Any lag-2+ opponent or own-sequence effect on labels beyond the pooled lag curves.
own_inferences: As posed ('large enough to drive AVOID labels'), the claim is likely false for most play types, since 0.01-0.02 PPP is small versus typical direct PPP gaps; it could matter only for play types whose direct PPP lies within ~0.02 of the AVOID cutoff.

Own-sequence lag effects will probably appear only as team-quality/pace/score-state confounds unless estimated within team-season; the decision-relevant claim should be that lag adjustments should NOT enter labels, with SPOT_UP lag-1 as the one pre-specified exception to check.

The question is best reframed as a label-stability/sensitivity analysis (flip rate under downstream adjustment) rather than an effect-existence test; with n in the tens of thousands per play type, significance is uninformative and effect-size thresholds must carry the decision.

Some opponent T+1 effect is mechanical (after a make the opponent inbounds against a set defense; after turnovers/misses the transition mix changes), so conditioning on the outcome of possession T creates floors and definitional effects. Estimates should condition on possession-start type.
uncertainties: The AVOID label definition and threshold are not given in the task or retrieved records and must be fixed before analysis.
Whether derived play-type labels in the graph database are stable across seasons and rebuilds (initiation_type mapping 0.7% in FAM:SF-CHT-025).
2025-26 playoffs are partial on the question date (complete only from 2026-06-21); 2025-26 regular season completeness depends on data version.
The control sets used in FAM:SF-APPS-075 are not visible in the retrieved summary; full text via read_family was not consulted.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, the claim could have been tested as a simple effect-existence question and likely 'proceeded'. The records show the T+1 effect is only ~0.01-0.02 PPP, own-team lag effects are recorded artifacts, and labels have foul leakage, so I narrowed the design to a pre-specified label-flip sensitivity analysis with within-team baselines, foul-adjusted PPP, effect-size thresholds, and a holdout season, and I lowered the prior of 'supported'.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type and AVOID labels depend on outcomes (foul endings, makes/turnovers), and T+1 conditioning on possession-T outcome introduces definitional effects; must be handled by foul-adjusted PPP and conditioning on possession-start type.

Play-type derivation has known leakage (OTHER 36% fouls; DRIVE 12pp below foul benchmark) and an unspecified AVOID rule; the analysis is only interpretable if labels are frozen and the rule is pre-specified.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work recorded small opponent T+1 suppression (~0.01-0.02 PPP, 4/8 play types real; FAM:SF-APPS-075) and artifact-status own-team lag effects that vanish within team (FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-CHT-029). No retrieved record tests whether these shifts change AVOID labels, so the label-impact part of the question remains open.

risks.text: Play-type PPP includes foul endings (OTHER 36%, PNR 22%) and AVOID labels inherit this; T+1 depends on how possession T ended (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPS-078).
Live turnovers raise opponent possession count and transition share by construction; makes versus misses change next-possession start state (FAM:SF-APPS-078 notes this as largely definitional).
Team quality, pace, score state, lineup and garbage time confound both lag and opponent T+1 estimates; pooled lag lifts vanished after team-season demeaning (FAM:SF-APPS-073, FAM:SF-CHT-029).
Play-type labels have foul leakage and low initiation_type mapping (0.7%); misclassification can distort play-type PPP and label thresholds.
8 play types x lags x opponent-play-type x seasons creates many comparisons; earlier sequential studies lacked correction (FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPM-022).
Large pooled n makes tiny effects 'significant' (d~0.01-0.03); team-by-play-type or star cells are small (n 30-95 in earlier cells).
Single-possession PPP is very noisy (SD ~1.1-1.2), so a 0.01-0.02 shift is small relative to per-cell sampling error; split-half reliability of label membership is unknown.
Season-to-season changes in pace, rules and play-type mix and the derived-labels pipeline may shift effects (flagged for FAM:SF-APPA-050).
Play types labeled AVOID because they have extreme low PPP will regress; selecting on extremes and then measuring downstream effects overstates labels' persistence.

design.estimand: For each play type X, (a) delta_down(X) = opponent T+1 PPP after the team runs X minus a matched within-team-season baseline for equal possession-start type; (b) delta_lag(X,k) = own-team PPP at lag k after X minus the within-team-season baseline; (c) label-flip rate: share of play types (and of team x play-type cells with n>=min) whose AVOID classification changes when direct PPP is replaced by direct PPP + delta_down (and + delta_lag). 'Drives AVOID labels' is judged on (c), not on p-values.
design.unit: Possession pair (T, T+1) for opponent effects; own-team possession sequence (T, T+k) for lags; analysed at play-type and team-season-by-play-type level.
design.sample: Discovery: 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular seasons. Holdout: 2025-26 regular season (use only the version marked complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs reported separately as secondary; 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete (2026-06-21) and then analysed once. Exclude garbage time, end-of-period possessions, possessions after timeouts/dead-ball resets handled as a separate stratum, and OTHER labelled play type from primary labels (reported as sensitivity).
design.power: Pooled play-type n is in the tens to hundreds of thousands (n>150k per lag in FAM:SF-CHT-029), so power is ample at play-type level: SE of PPP difference ~0.003-0.006. Equivalence margin of +/-0.02 PPP (about the size of the previously recorded effects) must be fixed in advance; team-level cells are underpowered (few hundred possessions, SE ~0.06+) and should be treated as descriptive with shrinkage. Report CIs, not only p-values.
design.controls: Within-team-season baselines (team fixed effects, ideally also opponent fixed effects); possession-start type (live TO, miss, make, dead ball); score margin, period, clock bucket, lineup/starter state, home/away, pace; foul-ending-adjusted PPP (separate foul-ending bucket per FAM:SF-CHT-025) and shot-quality-neutral sensitivity; condition on possession-T outcome or report both marginal and outcome-stratified effects to separate mechanical effects.
design.falsification: Placebo: randomly permute play-type labels within team-season-game-period strata and recompute delta_down and flip rates; real effects must exceed the 95% placebo range. Negative-control: lag/downstream effect for a non-adjacent possession (T+3 for opponent), and decay sanity (lag-1 >= lag-2) per the FAM:SF-CHT-029 gate. Use season-holdout replication; effects with opposite sign in holdout are declared failures.
design.multiplicity: Families defined in advance (8 play types x opponent T+1; 8 x lags 1-5); Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05 within each family; star/team-level cells exploratory only and not used for labels; no post-hoc cell mining.
design.decision_rule: Conclude 'downstream effect drives AVOID labels' only if, in discovery AND holdout, (i) delta_down CI for the play type excludes zero after BH and its lower bound exceeds the 0.02 PPP equivalence margin, AND (ii) the label-flip rate is >=20% of play types (or the effect exceeds the distance to the AVOID cutoff for at least one play type), AND (iii) the placebo and decay checks pass. If delta_down CIs lie within +/-0.02 and flip rate <10%, conclude 'does not drive labels' (rejected). For own-sequence lags, conclude 'lags matter' only if within-team lag-1 effects exceed the margin and decay; otherwise do not include lags in labels. Mixed results: report as inconclusive.
design.data_version: Freeze per-game NBA stats API play-by-play and the derived play-type possession records (graph database) with the build hash/date as of 2026-06-19; record label-derivation code version; 2025-26 regular season data complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs deferred until complete (2026-06-21), and any rebuild of derived labels requires re-registration.

methodological_questions: Is opponent next-possession PPP after a play type large enough to drive AVOID labels?
Do lagged own-team possession sequences affect play-type efficiency estimates after controlling for confounders?
How do outcome-derived labels, mechanical floors, and selection effects confound next-possession and lag analyses?
args.query: Does opponent next-possession PPP after running a play type, and own-sequence lags, materially drive AVOID labels in play-type labeling?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
